name: Asahel
description: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy

points: Asahel, one of the three sons of Zeruiah, was as light of foot as a wild roe, meaning he was fast, and he pursued Abner and would not turn aside. Abner warned him again and again to turn off and take another man's armor, not wanting to have to kill him and face Joab his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: When Asahel refused to turn aside, Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear under the fifth rib, and he died there. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. Those who came to the place stood still; the lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Joab, without David's knowledge, sent messengers after Abner and brought him back to Hebron, took him aside in the gate to speak quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 3: The House of David Waxes Stronger

points: The rest of the thirty are named: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and the others down to Uriah the Hittite, thirty and seven in all. Some carry names like Zelek the Ammonite and Uriah the Hittite, but this does not mean they were Hamites in David's army; it means they dwelt in those lands after Israel removed the nations from the coasts.

note.label: 2 Samuel 23: The Last Words of David and His Mighty Men

points: The sons of Zeruiah, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, are named, and Amasa the son of Abigail, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: The roll of the valiant men of the armies follows, including Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan of Bethlehem, and many more named men from across the tribes.
